texts.https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/cumhu:
Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan,, COP31 Liderler Zirvesi 'ne ilişkin yaptığı yazılı açıklamada, Antalya'da düzenlenen COP31 Liderler Zirvesi'ne katılan tüm devlet ve hükümet başkanlarına en derin şükranlarını sundu.
Uluslararası alanda büyük sınamaların yaşandığı bir dönemde, bir araya gelmelerinin ve mesajlarını bizzat iletmelerinin özel bir önem taşıdığını vurgulayan Erdoğan, şu değerlendirmelerde bulundu:
"Burada bulunmanız, iklime yönelik siyasi taahhüdünüzü ve karşı karşıya olduğumuz sınamaların işbirliğiyle üstesinden gelebileceğimize olan inancınızı ortaya koymuştur. Zirveye aktif katkılarından ötürü tüm taraflara, uluslararası kuruluşlara, çok taraflı kalkınma bankalarına ve paydaşlara da teşekkür ediyorum. Ortaya koyduğunuz yaklaşımlar ve sürece yapıcı şekilde müdahil olma arzunuz, COP31 çalışmalarını güçlü şekilde yüreklendirdi. Başkanlığımız, bu ruhu tüm tarafların çekincelerini ve önceliklerini gözeterek daha da ileriye taşıyacaktır. Paris Anlaşması'nın ikinci on yılına girdiğimiz bu dönemde, gerçekleştirdiğimiz fikir alışverişleri, iklim değişikliğiyle mücadele etmenin hem bilimsel hem de ahlaki bir zorunluluk olduğunu yeniden teyit etmiştir. Sorumluluğumuz, yaşamları halihazırda etkilenmiş olan tüm insanlara, gelecek nesillere ve gerek toplumlarımızın gerek ekonomilerimizin bağlı olduğu dünyamıza kadar uzanmaktadır.
Görüşmelerde ortaya çıkan geniş ortak zemin beni cesaretlendirdi. Ülkeler Antalya'ya farklı deneyimler, öncelikler ve ulusal koşullarla geldiler; bununla birlikte bu farklılıklar ortak bir zeminin tesisine engel olmadı. Bu ortam, COP31 boyunca ve sonrasında devam edecek diyalog ve işbirliği için kıymetli bir temel oluşturmaktadır."
"ELEKTRİFİKASYON, YEŞİL SANAYİLEŞME VE SÜRDÜRÜLEBİLİR KALKINMA..."
Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan, ortak zeminin COP31 Eylem Gündemi'nin önceliklerine yansıtılmış olmasının özellikle cesaret verici olduğunu aktardı.
Zirve sırasında düzenlenen üst düzey etkinliklerin, elektrifikasyon, uygulama, yeşil sanayileşme, dayanıklılık, sıfır atık ve iklim finansmanı konularının etraflıca tartışılmasına imkan sağladığına dikkati çeken Erdoğan, şu ifadeleri kullandı:
"Gerçekleştirilen etkinlikler ayrıca, Afrika, Pasifik ve diğer bölgelerin önceliklerine de dikkat çekerek, iklim eylemini kalkınma ihtiyaçlarına ve ulusal koşullara yanıt verecek şekilde ilerletmenin önemini vurguladı. Son dönemde yaşanan doğal afetler ve can kayıpları ile geçim kaynaklarının yok olması, çalışmalarımızın insanlık açısından aciliyetini ortaya koymaktadır. Bundan etkilenen topluluklar ve onların iyileşme süreçlerini destekleyenlerle dayanışma içinde olduğumu ifade etmek isterim. Bu toplulukların tecrübeleri, iklim risklerine karşı daha güçlü erken uyarı sistemleri ve iklim risklerine en çok maruz kalanların daha iyi korunması da dahil olmak üzere, azaltımın yanı sıra dirençlilik ve uyumun artırılmasının öneminin altını çizmektedir. Elektrifikasyon, yeşil sanayileşme ve sürdürülebilir kalkınmanın sunduğu fırsatları değerlendirirken odağımızda bu meseleler olmalıdır."
Erdoğan, COP31 Zirvesi'nin ayrıca, en çok ihtiyaç duyanlar için finansmana erişimin önemini vurguladığını, bu nedenle "İklim Uygulama Köprüsü"nün büyük destek gördüğünü dile getirdi.
Mekanizmanın amacının ülkeler, finans kuruluşları ve taraflar arasında daha yakın işbirliği yoluyla mevcut taahhütleri somut sonuçlara dönüştürmek ve uyum, direnç ve sürdürülebilir kalkınma konularında ülkelerin önderliğinde yürütülen eylemlere destek sağlamak olduğunu belirten Erdoğan, şunları kaydetti:
"COP31, uygulama odaklı bir COP olarak tasarlandı. Bu doğrultuda, '35x35 Küresel Elektrifikasyon Taahhüdü'ne verilen destekten memnuniyet duyuyoruz. Zirve boyunca pek çok lider elektrifikasyonun sunduğu fırsatları dile getirdi ve birçok ülke şimdiden bu girişimin parçası oldu. Ülkelerin kendi ihtiyaç ve önceliklerine uygun yollar izleyerek elektrifikasyonu yaygınlaştırmaları, enerji güvenliğine ve kalkınmaya katkıda bulunabilecektir. COP31 Eylem Gündemi'ne liderliğimiz vasıtasıyla uygulamaya daha fazla siyasi önem kazandırmayı ve hükümetler ile paydaşları pratik çözümler etrafında bir araya getirmeyi amaçladık. Paris Anlaşması'nın uygulanmasında ilerleme kaydederken, Başkanlığımızın kalıcı bir katkısının da ulusal öncelikleri belirleyenler ile bunların gerçekleştirilmesine yardımcı olanlar arasında daha yakın bir işbirliğinin tesis edilmesi olmasını ümit ediyoruz."
"SÜRDÜRÜLEBİLİR UYGULAMALAR, TOPLUMUN HER KESİMİNİN KATKISINI GEREKTİRECEK"
Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan , Türkiye ile Avustralya arasındaki ortaklığın çok taraflılığa duyulan güvenin bir ifadesi olduğunu bildirdi.
Birbirinden coğrafi olarak uzak; farklı koşullar ve sınamalara sahip ülkeleri bir araya getiren bu modelin ortak bir amaç doğrultusunda işbirliği yapmanın önemini ortaya koyduğuna işaret eden Erdoğan, şu görüşlere yer verdi:
"Bu ortaklıktan ve özellikle Pre-COP ev sahipleri Tuvalu ve Fiji başta olmak üzere Pasifik Ada ülkelerinin COP31 sürecine katılımından memnuniyet duyuyorum. Sürdürülebilir uygulamalar, toplumun her kesiminin katkısını gerektirecektir. Hükümetler; ulusal öncelikler ve politikalar aracılığıyla yönlendirme sağlarken, işletmeler, finans kuruluşları, yerel yönetimler ve sivil toplum bu öncelikleri eyleme dönüştürmeye yardımcı olabilecek kaynak, uzmanlık ve deneyimi sunmaktadır. Sürece katılımlarını ve Eylem Gündemi'nin ülkelerin öncülüğünde şekillenen çabaları desteklemek için sunduğu işbirliği fırsatlarını memnuniyetle karşılıyorum. Devam eden müzakerelerde, tüm tarafları Liderler Zirvesi'nin yapıcı ruhunu sürdürmeye teşvik ediyorum. Antalya'da sergilenen siyasi taahhüt, Paris Anlaşması kapsamında yürütülecek çalışmalar bakımından cesaret verici niteliktedir. Bu kararlılığımızı sürdürelim, uygulama yönündeki çabalarımızı devam ettirelim ve 1,5 derece hedefini ulaşılabilir kılalım."

COP31'in uygulama odaklı bir konferans olarak tasarlandığını vurgulayan Erdoğan, "35x35 Küresel Elektrifikasyon Taahhüdü"ne verilen destekten memnuniyet duyduğunu ifade etti.
Zirve boyunca çok sayıda liderin elektrifikasyonun sunduğu fırsatlara dikkati çektiğini ve birçok ülkenin girişime katıldığını belirten Erdoğan, elektrik kullanımının yaygınlaştırılmasının enerji güvenliğine ve ekonomik kalkınmaya katkıda bulunabileceğini söyledi.
Erdoğan, ülkelerin bu dönüşümü kendi ihtiyaçları ve ulusal öncelikleri doğrultusunda gerçekleştirmesinin önemine işaret etti.
Açıklamasında son dönemde meydana gelen doğal afetlere ve can kayıplarına da değinen Erdoğan, yaşanan felaketlerin iklim değişikliğiyle mücadelede zaman kaybedilmemesi gerektiğini ortaya koyduğunu belirtti.
Afetlerden etkilenen topluluklarla dayanışma mesajı veren Erdoğan, iklim risklerine karşı daha güçlü erken uyarı sistemlerinin kurulması ve kırılgan toplulukların korunması gerektiğini vurguladı.
Emisyonların azaltılmasının yanı sıra iklim değişikliğine uyum ve dirençliliğin artırılmasının da öncelikli hedefler arasında bulunması gerektiğini ifade etti.
COP31 sürecinde Türkiye ile Avustralya arasında kurulan ortaklığa da değinen Erdoğan, bu iş birliğinin çok taraflılığa duyulan güvenin bir göstergesi olduğunu belirtti.
Coğrafi açıdan birbirinden uzak ve farklı koşullara sahip ülkelerin ortak bir amaç etrafında buluşmasının önemine dikkati çeken Erdoğan, özellikle COP31 öncesi toplantılara ev sahipliği yapan Tuvalu ve Fiji başta olmak üzere Pasifik Ada ülkelerinin sürece katılımından duyduğu memnuniyeti dile getirdi.
İklim politikalarının uygulanabilmesi için hükümetlerin yanı sıra özel sektör, finans kuruluşları, yerel yönetimler ve sivil toplumun da sürece katılması gerektiğini belirten Erdoğan, COP31 Eylem Gündemi'nin bu kesimler arasındaki iş birliğini güçlendirmesini hedeflediklerini ifade etti.
Devam eden müzakerelerde ülkeleri Liderler Zirvesi'nde ortaya konulan yapıcı yaklaşımı sürdürmeye davet eden Erdoğan, açıklamasını şu sözlerle tamamladı:
"Antalya'da sergilenen siyasi taahhüt, Paris Anlaşması kapsamında yürütülecek çalışmalar bakımından cesaret verici niteliktedir. Bu kararlılığımızı sürdürelim, uygulama yönündeki çabalarımızı devam ettirelim ve 1,5°C hedefini ulaşılabilir kılalım."

Jensen Huang stepped down as the chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday, four days after the company announced its internal investigation into an affair he had with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.
“Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately,” the Nvidia board said in a statement. Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, will serve as interim CEO. The board said it “will consider internal and external candidates” for a permanent replacement.
The board’s investigation was announced on November 8, slightly less than two weeks after The New York Times reported that the chief executive had been the target of a Chinese intelligence operation facilitated through his relationship with Alice Huang, who has no known relation to Jensen. The pair have been spotted in public together at least twice, in June 2024 and May 2025 . On November 11, The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also allegedly had a relationship with a direct report at Nvidia.
The alleged relationship with a subordinate, along with Huang’s business dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI company where Alice Huang previously held a senior position, likely played a greater role in the board’s decision to oust Huang than the Chinese espionage allegations, a source familiar with the matter tells WIRED.
US intelligence officials reportedly briefed President Donald Trump on Huang’s relationship with Alice last year, but the president did not act on it. On November 6, The New York Times and Financial Times reported that Alice was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security and that she had been recruited to collect information on the Nvidia executive. (The Chinese government has rejected all claims that Alice was a spy for the country. )
Huang sent a companywide email on Sunday acknowledging his affair, apologizing to his family and Nvidia employees, and pledging cooperation with the internal investigation. The executive has been married to his wife, Lori Huang, since 1985 , and both of the couple’s two children work at the company.
On Monday, WIRED exclusively reported that last year Huang began working with a crisis PR firm to manage his personal communications. In October 2025, those PR consultants started to be looped in on all press inquiries involving Huang, whether those inquiries were personal or professional in nature.
The timing lines up with a New York Times report that month that the US Commerce Department was investigating whether Alice Huang’s Megaspeed was helping Chinese companies get around American export controls with the help of a vast web of subsidiaries. The investigation was reportedly halted and transferred to the Justice Department after Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter inquired about it.
Huang has been a vocal critic of these export controls, which he argues unnecessarily constrain the market for American chips, create discrete Chinese and American tech ecosystems, and spur China to build competitive chips of its own. Huang has worked to develop a relationship with Trump in order to advocate for policies that are advantageous for Nvidia, including the idea of opening its markets to China.
Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 with friends Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. The trio reportedly brainstormed their vision for the company in a Denny’s diner and aspired to bring realistic 3D graphics to personal computers. For the first few decades of its existence, Nvidia was primarily known in the gaming community for creating chips powerful enough to render high-quality in-game graphics.
In 2012, after a new kind of neural network known as AlexNet won a high-profile prize in computer vision, Nvidia pivoted from high-speed computer graphics to building chips that would support artificial intelligence. Huang has repeatedly said that the introduction of AlexNet, which was developed by AI engineers Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton, was a “Big Bang”–like event for computing.
Because its new GPUs proved highly effective at powering AI models that require massive amounts of processing power, the value of Nvidia shares soared in 2023 and 2024, in lockstep with the broader AI boom that began sweeping through the world economy. In the summer of 2025, Nvidia became the first company in history to cross $4 trillion in value.
As of September 2026, the company controlled about 90 percent of the GPU market. Much of Nvidia’s epic rise over the few decades has been attributed not just to its cutting-edge chips and its software “moat,” CUDA, that keeps developers locked into those chips, but also to the fast-thinking, controlling, charismatic, and often bombastic leadership style of Huang himself. Now, that critical part of the company’s success is out.

Nvidia’s CEO and cofounder Jensen Huang is officially out , and longtime chief financial officer Colette Kress is in. The chipmaker’s board of directors announced Thursday that Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013, has been named interim CEO following Huang’s resignation amid a scandal over his extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman believed by US officials to be an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.
Harvey Jones, the newly appointed chair of Nvidia’s board, said in a statement that Kress “has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position.” He added that Kress will be supported by an “experienced leadership team” and that the board has “full confidence” in her.
Kress was among the most obvious candidates to fill the void after Huang’s departure, according to multiple tech executives and industry analysts who follow Nvidia closely, given her long tenure at the company, credibility on Wall Street and across the tech industry, and, perhaps most importantly, her deep familiarity with Nvidia’s business and finances.
“She’s extremely strong-willed, professional, and whip-smart. She doesn’t tolerate nonsense. She can be friendly and gracious too,” says a former Nvidia executive who spoke on the condition of anonymity. “She obviously has a keen sense for how Jensen thinks.”
“Colette is the logical choice,” says Patrick Moorhead, founder and chief analyst at Moor Insights & Strategies, who has tracked the chip industry for decades. “She has credibility with investors because she answers hard questions directly.”
Moorhead says Kress has operated as much more than a “numbers” CFO. “In my conversations with her, she goes deep on the product road map, from rack-scale systems to networking and software,” he says.
Nvidia’s board said on Sunday it was launching an independent investigation into Huang’s activities following a report by The New York Times that he had an affair with a woman named Alice Huang, who US officials suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. WIRED reported on Monday that Huang quietly hired a crisis communications firm sometime last year to handle matters related to his personal life. By October of 2025, the firm was being looped in on all press inquiries involving Huang at Nvidia, around the same time The New York Times reported that US authorities were investigating whether a company linked to Alice Huang had helped Chinese firms evade US chip export controls through its subsidiaries.
While Huang has long been the public face of Nvidia, Kress has been responsible for managing the chipmaker’s relationship with Wall Street. On earnings calls, she often details Nvidia’s financial performance, customer demand, supply constraints, and other key metrics.
“One of the things we don’t focus on is the stock price. We focus on our investors and how we would like to innovate,” Kress told the Israeli business newspaper Globes in 2023.
Before joining Nvidia, Kress spent more than two decades in finance roles at Microsoft, Cisco, and Texas Instruments. Huang personally recruited her in 2013, when Nvidia was still best known for its gaming graphics cards, according to Globes. Huang laid out his vision for the company’s future on a whiteboard, explaining how Nvidia could become a major supplier of computing infrastructure for artificial intelligence.
Other potential successors to Huang included Ian Buck, an Nvidia veteran of more than 20 years who created the company’s software platform CUDA and now oversees its high-performance computing business, and Jeff Fisher, who joined Nvidia in 1994 as the head of software sales and later became senior vice president of its GeForce unit, where he led Nvidia’s strategy for bringing GPUs to market.
However, Nvidia’s unusual corporate structure has long meant that dozens of executives reported directly to Huang. The company lacks a traditional chief operating officer. Even executive vice presidents aren’t necessarily given direct control over budgets, sources have told WIRED. As a result, few people within the organization have the same level of understanding of the company’s financials as Kress.
The former Nvidia executive who spoke to WIRED on the condition of anonymity said that while Kress is incredibly sharp and “can step into the [CEO] role immediately without needing any guidance,” she doesn’t have the same engineering and technical expertise that Huang brought to the role. She has also shied away from being “at the center of public attention,” the person said.
Given the intense scrutiny surrounding Huang lately, that leadership style might be a welcome temporary change for Nvidia.

Kahramanmaraş merkezli 6 Şubat 2023 depremlerinde Gaziantep'in Nizip ilçesinde yıkılan Furkan Apartmanı'na ilişkin yargı sürecinde önemli bir gelişme yaşandı. Binanın çökmesi sonucu 51 kişinin hayatını kaybettiği olayla ilgili davada, Gaziantep Bölge Adliye Mahkemesi 16. Ceza Dairesi'nin ikinci bozma kararının ardından dosya yeniden ele alındı.
İstinaf Dairesi, önceki yargılamada çelişkili bilirkişi raporlarının giderilmemesi, bazı tanıkların dinlenmemesi ve kamu görevlisi sanıklar bakımından bilinçli taksir hükümlerinin değerlendirilmemesi nedeniyle eksik inceleme yapıldığına hükmetti.
Daire ayrıca, binanın fiili müteahhidinin Hasan Hüseyin Sever olduğuna dikkat çekerek hakkındaki beraat kararını hatalı buldu. Fenni mesul Yılmaz Şahin Yurtyapan'a verilen cezanın belirlenmesinde de hukuka aykırılık bulunduğunu değerlendirdi. Binanın yıkılmasına yol açan kusurların ve sanıkların sorumluluk oranlarının uzman bilirkişi heyeti tarafından ayrı ayrı tespit edilmesini istedi.
ANKA Haber Ajansı'nın edindiği bilgilere göre Nizip Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi, istinafın bozma kararının ardından dosyayı yeniden değerlendirdi.
Mahkeme heyeti, müteahhit Hasan Hüseyin Sever'in tutuklanmasına yönelik yakalama emri düzenlenmesine hükmetti. Fenni mesul Yılmaz Şahin Yurtyapan ile iş yeri sahibi Eyüp Öğüt'ün tutukluluk hallerinin sürmesine karar verildi.
Diğer iş yeri sahibi Faik Öğüt hakkında daha önce çıkarılan tutuklamaya yönelik yakalama emrinin de devamına hükmeden mahkeme, dosyadaki eksikliklerin giderilmesi amacıyla yeni bir bilirkişi raporu alınmasını kararlaştırdı.
Davanın bir sonraki duruşması 21 Ocak 2027 tarihinde görülecek.
Furkan Apartmanı'nın yıkılmasıyla ilgili davada müteahhitler Abdullah Devrim Sever ve Hasan Hüseyin Sever, fenni mesul Yılmaz Şahin Yurtyapan ile binanın altında bulunan iş yerinin sahipleri Faik Öğüt, Eyüp Öğüt ve Nejdet Alpay sanıklar arasında bulunuyor.
Enkazdan yaralı kurtarılan ve binanın altındaki iş yerinde çalışan Coşkun Şahin ile kardeşi Ömer Şahin de aynı dosyada yargılanıyor. Bu sanıklar hakkında, birden fazla kişinin ölümüne ve yaralanmasına neden olma suçundan bilinçli taksir kapsamında dava açıldı.
Binaya ilişkin yapı kullanma izin belgesinde imzası bulunan dönemin Nizip Belediyesi İmar Müdürü Mehmet Aslan, İmar İşleri Müdür Yardımcısı Orhan Zoroğlu ile inşaat mühendisleri Oktay Aktaş ve Bülent Bilici ise birden fazla kişinin ölümüne ve yaralanmasına neden olma suçlamasıyla taksir kapsamında yargılanıyor.
51 kişinin yaşamını yitirdiği faciaya ilişkin davada, yeni bilirkişi raporunun ve yapılacak yargılamanın ardından ortaya çıkacak sonuç merakla bekleniyor.

The Nvidia Board of Directors announced on Thursday morning that the company’s co-founder and CEO of 33 years, Jensen Huang, has resigned as president, CEO, and member of the board, effective immediately.
This is a shocking twist for one of the most valuable companies in the world, which designs the chips that make the AI boom possible. Few people would have predicted this turn of events even just a week ago, as Huang has been so central to Nvidia throughout the company’s existence that he never even established a succession plan . But Huang has now been ousted after reports that he had affairs with both an alleged Chinese spy and one of his direct reports at Nvidia.
While the company conducts a more thorough search for Huang’s successor, Nvidia CFO and Executive Vice President Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO. But beyond her name and job title, what do we know about the person who will now lead a company worth about $3.8 trillion?
According to Nvidia’s website , Kress has worked at the company since September 2013. Before that, she spent three years as an SVP and CFO of Cisco’s Business Technology Operations Finance organization. She also worked at Microsoft for 13 years, where she spent four years as CFO of the Server and Tools division. She holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University.
The California-based 59-year-old has a very limited social media presence — on Linkedin , she has commented some well wishes on former colleagues’ posts about their retirement. But as CFO, she’s been a regular presence on Nvidia’s earnings calls, making her a familiar figure for analysts covering the company.
According to Forbes’ list of America’s Richest Self-Made Women, Kress’ net worth is estimated to be about $1.2 billion. Her Forbes profile adds that she initially joined Nvidia in part because her two sons endorsed the company for its role in the video game industry, which it was best known for at the time.
“Nvidias strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” Kress said in a statement . “We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.”
Nvidia is slated to report its quarterly earnings on Tuesday, when we will likely hear more from Kress about her plans for the company’s immediate future.

Microsoft said its Outlook email service is currently experiencing an outage, preventing both business and consumer users from accessing their inboxes.
The issue was initially flagged as affecting the U.S. and the Americas, and later expanded to affect “any region.”
Microsoft hasn’t given a specific cause, but said that it was providing updates in its admin center , which wasn’t reachable at the time of publication. In a post on X for users who can’t access the admin center, Microsoft said some of its infrastructure was experiencing “elevated load,” and that it was “redistributing connection traffic across our broader worldwide infrastructure to help balance the load.”
In its latest update, Microsoft attributed this incident to “a large number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable,” for reasons it did not explain. Microsoft said it continues to investigate the outage.
Microsoft says its video conferencing tool Teams, file sharing platform SharePoint, and its AI tool Copilot are also unavailable. The company says its Defender XDR security system is also affected by the outage.
Consumers are also unable to access their OneDrive storage, Office (for the web), and several other Microsoft services during the ongoing outage.
TechCrunch will reach out to Microsoft for comment, as soon as our own email service has resumed.
The company’s last major incident was in September , when a days-long outage hit Microsoft 365, its online productivity suite that includes Outlook. During that outage, Microsoft blamed a “core authentication configuration” issue that prevented users from accessing the service.

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has resigned following revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, plunging the chipmaker at the heart of the global AI boom into crisis.
The 63-year-old will be replaced by chief financial officer Colette Kress, who will serve as interim chief executive.
His exit comes after he admitted to having a relationship with a woman that US authorities believe was a Chinese spy. It also emerged on Wednesday that Huang had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive.
Nvidia shares were down more than 10 percent in pre-market trading, extending earlier losses after the announcement of Huang’s resignation.
Huang, who cofounded Nvidia in 1993, led it to become what was until recently the world’s most valuable company.
Huang’s departure marks a startling end to his more than 33-year tenure, during which Nvidia evolved from a small video-game chip company into the linchpin of the global AI infrastructure boom.
Huang has become one of the most recognizable figures in tech, as Nvidia’s semiconductors became integral to training and running AI systems such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude.
Nvidia stock extended its pre-market decline after the company announced that Jensen Huang had resigned as chief executive.
Shares were down 10.2 percent in pre-market trading, a move that would wipe off more than $400 billion in market capitalization.

Microsoft 365 issues have been cutting people off from their email since early Thursday afternoon, and they still aren’t fixed.
Since just before 1PM ET on Thursday, reports have come in from around the world that people can’t access their Outlook email, either through the web or apps. Microsoft quickly acknowledged the issue from its Microsoft 365 Status account , saying that “We’ve determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors.”
There were also some reports of problems with Teams, but not to the same extent, while Microsoft’s official updates said customers may experience issues across its suite of 365 business services. Microsoft comms director Ben Hope said in a statement that “We are aware and investigating reports of users experiencing issues with Microsoft 365 services, primarily issues with Exchange Online. We appreciate our customers’ patience while we work to restore services as soon as possible.”
Several hours later, Microsoft has gone through several variations of update notes regarding the issues and its attempts to fix them, saying it’s had problems rebooting servers and being able to monitor their health. As of about 6PM ET, Microsoft has a note saying it’s managed to get some of the affected servers running:
We’ve begun returning a portion of the affected servers to service, and they’re remaining stable so far. We’ve also shifted traffic and connections to alternative pathways wherever possible and have observed limited recovery in some regions.
We’ve streamlined our recovery process to expedite returning the remaining affected servers to service. To further support recovery, we’re implementing protective traffic management measures in a specific location to reduce load on the affected infrastructure, and we’ll expand these measures to additional locations if we observe positive results. As capacity is restored, users may experience a gradual recovery as their clients reconnect to the service.
There’s still no ETA for full restoration, but we will continue to monitor this ongoing outage.

It’s not just you. Microsoft’s 365 business and enterprise services suffered a major outage on Thursday, preventing users of its popular cloud suite from accessing their accounts.
Around 10:40 am ET on Thursday, Microsoft posted on its 365 status page on X that it was “investigating reports of users experiencing issues when accessing or using Microsoft Teams functionality in North America.” By just before 1 pm ET, it said it was aware of “issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas.”
Microsoft later said that its network was also “experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors,” but that the issue was related to servers going offline, not due to increased traffic.
Around an hour later, Microsoft said it had “begun redistributing connection traffic across our broader worldwide infrastructure to help balance the load” and was “aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact.”
“We've paused all deployments. We're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure, and we're restarting affected servers to return them to service,” Microsoft wrote.
In an update on its status page , Microsoft said impacted services may include Exchange Online, Microsoft Teams, SharePoint Online, Microsoft Copilot 365, and Microsoft Defender XDR.
“We are aware and investigating reports of users experiencing issues with Microsoft 365 services, primarily issues with Exchange Online,” a Microsoft spokesperson tells WIRED in a statement. “We appreciate our customer's patience while we work to restore services as soon as possible.”
Outage reports on the service uptime tracking website Downdetector began falling around 1:15 pm ET after a large spike in users reporting issues with Outlook and other Microsoft 365 products around noon.
It is currently unclear when the outage may be over or what its cause may be. In a status update on X posted just before 3 pm ET, Microsoft said “a problem” was “causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable” but that it was attempting to reboot its systems to hopefully bring them back online.
Outages in cloud services occur frequently, and their causes can vary. Configuration errors, resolution issues with the Domain Name System, and cyberattacks can all cause connection errors. There is currently no indication that a cyberattack caused the current Microsoft outage.
While major Microsoft outages are relatively rare, they are far from unprecedented. In July 2024, a corrupted update from the security firm CrowdStrike caused the “blues screen of death” on Windows machines around the world, while a separate but nearly simultaneous outage knocked out Microsoft Azure services for hours , causing untold millions of dollars in lost revenue due to companies’ inability to function as normal.
Updated 11/12/2026 at 3:05 pm ET: Added comment from Microsoft.
Updated 11/12/2026 at 5:20 pm ET: WIRED updated the article to clarify that the Azure outage was unrelated to the CrowdStrike-related issues with Windows in 2024.

In the wake of the industry-shaking news of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation on Thursday, U.S. President Donald Trump is floating the idea that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over the position.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that “only one man” could take Huang’s place: Tim Cook of Apple.
Cook stepped down as Apple’s CEO on September 1, 2026, after 15 years running the company , but he’s still very much involved with Apple. While John Ternus took over as Apple’s CEO, Cook transitioned into the role of executive chairman of Apple’s board of directors, which sees him continuing to engage with global policymakers and manage international relationships, including Apple’s relations with China.
Trump is not the only one to suggest Cook as a replacement for Huang. Jeffrey Sonnenfeld , Senior Associate Dean for Leadership Studies at Yale School of Management, who studies CEO leadership and corporate governance, penned an op-ed in Time on Wednesday , suggesting Cook should be among the potential candidates. He wrote that Cook has “an unparalleled track record of succeeding a bigger-than-life founder,” in reference to Cook taking over from Apple founder Steve Jobs.
Whether or not Trump agrees with this opinion, or is simply blasting off an idea that hopped into his mind, is anyone’s guess.
“Tim Nvidia,” however, doesn’t quite have the same ring as “Tim Apple” does .

Recovery process under way, company says, after nearly 130,000 users worldwide reported access issues
Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams and other apps were disrupted for thousands of users for more than five hours on Thursday, with Microsoft saying it was still working to return affected servers to service, but had observed limited recovery.
A Microsoft spokesperson said the company “had no indication of a cyber-attack”.
Outage website Down Detector showed a spike in Microsoft 365 problems around 1pm ET, with nearly 130,000 reports of issues affecting access to Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams as well as enterprise services such as SharePoint and OneDrive. AI assistant Copilot was also affected.
New reports fell from that peak, to about 13,000 five hours later, but many said they couldn’t send and receive emails, or had trouble loading their inboxes altogether.
Earlier, Microsoft said that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” – which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors”. The company determined a number of servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” due to a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks.
Posting on X, Microsoft said it was “investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods”.
The company said the servers it had restored had remained stable so ‌far and that it was shifting traffic to alternate routes wherever possible while streamlining the process to bring the remaining affected servers back ​online.
“As capacity is restored, users may experience a gradual recovery as their clients reconnect,” the company said in a statement.
The Microsoft outage also hit connectors used by ⁠OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s AI ⁠services.
OpenAI said it was investigating an issue with Microsoft connectors in which new connections may be broken and tools were not working as ⁠expected. Anthropic said it had identified an issue with an upstream provider ​affecting its Microsoft 365 ​connector.
Microsoft last month reported an ​outage of its Azure cloud platform that affected ​suite of productivity software, ‌and a range ​of industries worldwide.
As the company worked to restart and validate affected servers, it said it was in parallel “assessing whether reverting the small number of recent configuration updates we identified could help accelerate recovery”.
Mark Gregory, associate professor in the School of Engineering at RMIT University, said the outage appears to be affecting the network layer in Microsoft’s systems, and was potentially similar to the configuration issue which brought down Optus’s network in 2023 .
He said when some of the servers have configuration issues, it means customers are forced to share a smaller pool of servers to access the cloud services.
“If you lose part of that pool, then all of the users are trying to access the remaining servers, and that overloads them. And then they go down.
“And so you end up with a cascading problem. Then it takes time to find the underlying problem, in this case, a misconfiguration in the network layer.”
Gregory said it showed companies should invest more in testing environments for configuration changes before deployment in the live network, and said businesses reliant on cloud services such as Microsoft 365 should have backup options.
“From a global perspective, there is someone somewhere that’s that’s been badly affected by this and you end up with lost productivity,” he said.
“They’re being left high and dry now … it then becomes important to have an alternative.
“Many people would keep a Gmail account, if their Microsoft goes down, they use Gmail. If Gmail goes down, they use Microsoft.”
Earlier, the company said it had “successfully restored” problems related to Microsoft Teams in North America, although some users continued to report connectivity issues.

Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanlığından yapılan açıklamaya göre, COP31 "Dayanıklı Şehirler ve Yapılı Çevre" temasıyla devam ediyor.
Bu kapsamda gerçekleştirilen ICBC 2. Bakanlar Toplantısı'nda, 53 üye ve 14 gözlemci ülkenin temsilcileri bir araya geldi.
Likya Salonu'nda yapılan toplantıya, Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakan Yardımcısı Ömer Bulut ile Toplu Konut İdaresi (TOKİ) Başkanı Mustafa Levent Sungur katıldı.
COP31 Başkanlığının 2035 Küresel Uygulama Hedefleri arasında yer alan bina sektöründe enerji kullanım yoğunluğunun yüzde 25 azaltılması başlığının ele alındığı toplantı, Mesleki Hizmetler Genel Müdürü Banu Aslan'ın moderatörlüğünde yapıldı.
Bina ve inşaat sektörünün iklim değişikliğiyle mücadeledeki rolü, küresel ölçekte enerji verimliliğinin artırılması ve düşük karbonlu yapılaşmaya yönelik ortak hedeflerin masaya yatırıldığı toplantıda, küresel ölçekte binalarda enerji verimliliğini artırmak ve iklim hedeflerine ulaşmak amacıyla hazırlanan Binalarda Enerji Verimliliği Antalya Mutabakatı, ICBC üyesi ülkelerin imzasına açıldı.
Böylece yapı sektöründe uluslararası işbirliğinin güçlendirilmesi ve ortak hedefler doğrultusunda somut adımlar atılması için yeni süreç başlatıldı.
Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakan Yardımcısı Bulut, toplantıda yaptığı konuşmada, enerji verimliliğini artırmanın ve bina sektörünü dönüştürmenin yalnızca çevresel bir gereklilik değil, aynı zamanda ekonomik ve sosyal bir zorunluluk olduğunu belirtti.
Küresel enerji tüketiminin ve sera gazı emisyonlarının yaklaşık üçte birinden bina sektörünün sorumlu olduğuna dikkati çeken Bulut, şu ifadeleri kullandı:
"Bina sektörü, aynı zamanda şehirlerimizin dayanıklılığı ve vatandaşlarımızın yaşam kalitesi açısından da kritik bir öneme sahiptir. Bu nedenle Türkiye olarak 2030'a kadar neredeyse sıfır emisyonlu ve iklime dayanıklı binaları yeni norm haline getirmeyi hedefleyen iklim değişikliği yaklaşımını, bu yüzyılın en kritik dönüşüm çağrılarından biri olarak görüyoruz. Antalya Mutabakatı kapsamında çevrenin korunması alanında müzakereleri devam eden anlaşma metnini hükümetlerarası bir anlaşma olacak şekilde yeniden düzenledik."
Türkiye'nin 2053'e kadar net sıfır emisyona ulaşma hedefini benimsediğini hatırlatan Bulut, bu vizyon doğrultusunda ülkenin uzun vadeli yeşil dönüşümüne rehberlik edecek Uzun Vadeli İklim Stratejisi'ni hazırladıklarını vurguladı.
Bulut, Türkiye'nin 2035'e kadar ulusal sera gazı emisyonlarını 643 milyon ton karbondioksit eşdeğeri ile sınırlandırmayı taahhüt ettiği İkinci Ulusal Katkı Beyanı'nın oluşturduğunu da sözlerine ekledi.
Öte yandan, "Dayanıklı Şehirler ve Yapılı Çevre" teması kapsamında Assos Özel Etkinlik Alanı'nda "Uluslararası Sürdürülebilir Binalar Yarışması" ödül töreni gerçekleştirildi.
Mesleki Hizmetler Genel Müdürlüğü ile Birleşmiş Milletler Çevre Programı ev sahipliğinde, Küresel Bina ve İnşaat İttifakı işbirliğiyle düzenlenen yarışmanın ödül töreninde, YeS Onur Ödülleri ile Dünya Enerji Tasarrufu Şampiyonası ödülleri sahiplerine verildi.
Törene, Bakan Yardımcıları Fatma Varank ile Ömer Bulut'un yanı sıra bakan yardımcısı düzeyinde 53 üye ülke ve 14 gözlemci ülkenin temsilcileri ile jüri üyeleri ve ödül sahipleri katıldı.
Farklı ülkelerden yaklaşık 1000 başvurunun değerlendirildiği yarışmada, sürdürülebilir yapılaşmaya katkı sunan 6 proje çeşitli kategorilerde ödüllendirildi.
Anadolu Ajansı web sitesinde, AA Haber Akış Sistemi (HAS) üzerinden abonelere sunulan haberler, özetlenerek yayımlanmaktadır. Abonelik için lütfen iletişime geçiniz.
Bu haberde bir hata mı var? Her türlü talep, şikâyet ve görüş için okur temsilcimize ulaşabilirsiniz.

Nvidia is looking for a new CEO, and President Trump says the former Apple CEO would be ‘a great candidate.’
Jensen Huang resigned this morning as Nvidia’s CEO following reports of affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Right now, the company is being led by its CFO on an interim basis. But President Donald Trump is already throwing around one person he thinks should take over the chipmaking giant: former Apple CEO Tim Cook, who stepped down from leading the company on September 1st and moved into an executive chairman role.
Shortly after Huang’s resignation was announced today, Trump posted his idea about Cook on Truth Social: “NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple,” Trump said . “A Legend replaces a Legend!”
In a new episode of Stephen A. Smith’s Straight Shooter podcast published today, Trump made his pitch for Cook again, saying that Apple “would never be what it is today” if Steve Jobs was still “around”:
Well, you know, the expression, Anybody can be replaced? So it’s very hard to replace him, but I had an idea this morning that I sort of just released: Tim Cook. He just sort of semi-retired from Apple. He’s done one of the greatest jobs in the history of business.
I think if Tim Cook, who built Apple… If Steve Jobs were around, Apple would never be what it is today. Tim Cook took a lot of these brilliant ideas and designs and everything else from Jobs and others, and he made it into one of the great companies of the world in a fairly short period. I think Tim Cook would be a great candidate to run Nvidia.
Apple and Nvidia didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment. Cook is well-known for his ongoing relationship with President Trump , including gifting the president a 24k gold and glass statue last year . (Trump, after Cook announced his transition plan earlier this year, posted a story about having “the head of Apple calling to ‘kiss my ass.’”)
During the podcast, Trump said he spoke to Huang yesterday and that Huang is “going through hell”:
Well, the big thing is, was the woman a spy, and I don’t know if that’s been determined yet, but if the woman was a spy, yes, if the woman was not a spy, perhaps it would be different.
But I can tell you this. Somehow, he’ll end up on his feet. I mean, I know him, I know him pretty well. I always thought of him as a fine man.
I spoke to him yesterday. He’s going through hell. What he feels most badly about is his wife and family. That’s what he is, really… that’s what he told me. I’m president, and he called me. And he said, What I’ve done to my wife and family is... That’s what he talked about.
Trump, on the podcast, called Huang a “tremendous talent.” Other tech leaders have also publicly supported Huang following his resignation.

Whoop , the maker of screen-less fitness bands, is launching a social network on Thursday that lets its members follow friends and family and share their health data.
The network, called Whoop Humans, will be rolled out in the Whoop app to members at every membership tier at no extra cost. Members can follow anyone on Whoop and choose what to share, from sleep and recovery to workouts and achievements. Followers can react and comment; members can also attach photos and commentary to their data. It’s all opt-in, CEO Will Ahmed tells us.
Whoop already has a social feature, Teams, which a little more than half its customers use, according to the company. But Teams is built around groups and leaderboards, and everyone in a group sees everyone else’s information. Humans is meant to be more intimate. Members decide who follows them and who sees what, so a trainer can track a set of clients without the clients seeing one another’s data, for example.
I found myself questioning how much a spouse wants to know about the other’s sleep score when Ahmed mentioned this particular scenario, so I asked him how else beta members used these newer social features. He said the company learned that people were more engaged when someone reported a low recovery score than a nearly perfect one, suggesting that the new feature may be particularly helpful for understanding when someone is struggling and might need attention.
Indeed, the bigger story here is where Whoop continues to be headed, which is into medical wellness. Like its most direct rival, Oura, the company is pushing faster and more aggressively into the wellness opportunity that an aging population presents.
Whoop had already added FDA-cleared ECG and atrial fibrillation detection, blood pressure insights, blood testing, and medical-record uploads. Asked if older customers are gravitating to Whoop, Ahmed said, without offering specifics, that Whoop has seen “huge growth” among people over 60 over the past 18 months. He also said his was among the first companies accepted into a Medicare program that reimburses qualifying wearables that can show they improve health outcomes, and that it now has Medicare members.
He added that he expects families to be big users of Humans. (You can imagine adult children checking in on aging parents.)
But the company’s efforts to be thought of as the “brand for personal health” raises questions, naturally, about privacy. Ahmed said members choose which metrics to share, can remove followers, and can switch on “stealth mode” to go dark for a few days without changing their settings. Activities marked sensitive aren’t shared by default, and Ahmed said health alerts and medical information aren’t shared at all. Members can also report any comment or photo that they deem disturbing, and the company said reported content is reviewed.
As for minors, Whoop’s minimum age is 13 for all members (higher in some countries), meaning customers of that age can share their data subject to consents and privacy settings. Asked whether a parent could follow a teenager’s data, he didn’t answer directly and pointed to the privacy controls.
Ahmed also said Whoop doesn’t sell member data. “Our product is not you; it’s the membership,” he said, adding that the company doesn’t license data to third parties.
He was candid about dealmaking. Asked about Oura’s announcement this week that it will pay $625 million for Counsel Health , a service offering on-demand physicians, Ahmed said he expects “more consolidation” among AI-focused, clinician-focused, and wearable companies, and that Whoop is always on the prowl. Its deep relationship with members, he said, puts it “in a position to be an acquirer.”
He was more guarded about the company’s own finances, declining to share revenue or say whether Whoop is profitable. He did say that the company now has about 1,200 employees, membership on its software platform has increased more than 70% a year for three years running, and that it expects to have nearly 4 million members by year-end.
As for an IPO (the company raised a very big round earlier this year), he said only that Whoop “will certainly IPO in the future.” He also wouldn’t comment on Oura, which shelved its own IPO of up to $2.2 billion in September citing market uncertainty.
In the meantime, Whoop is widening its reach. The company announced that its devices will be sold through Ulta stores beginning next March (around 500 locations of the beauty retailer to start, and a target to retail in more than a thousand stores eventually). Indeed, Ahmed said Whoop’s female audience has more than doubled from last year.
As for competition, in addition to Google’s new Fitbit Air band, Whoop may soon have to contend with Apple, which is reportedly developing a Whoop-style band . But Ahmed mostly shrugged off those concerns, suggesting that building a product doesn’t guarantee success. Instead, he said, Whoop’s job is to stay true to the “aspiring” people it serves.

Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos. The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.”
While Google’s frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are best at deep reasoning for hard problems, Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across a variety of agentic workflows, or tasks in which an AI carries out multiple steps on its own, the company explained in an announcement.
The idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do. Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, its previous fast model, but it’s still pretty smart, even beating the more powerful Gemini 4 Argon on one broad intelligence benchmark, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index , at its default high thinking level.
In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode.
In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly. This means people can ask their questions in their natural train of thought, including those that have multiple parts or that include highly specific requests. Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says. Because of its improvements and better ability to follow instructions and call the right tools, Hydrogen is able to more precisely address each part of a user’s question.
Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries. This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains.
The addition of Hydrogen to Search will also mean more images, structured responses, comparison tables, and custom tools will appear as visual responses to users’ queries in AI Mode.
Google also says Hydrogen can work on its own for everyday work in areas like writing code, running tests, or verifying code changes, or it can be paired with Carbon and Argon in workflows that combine several models.
The model offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high (default), and a new, extra-high tier (“xhigh”), all of which are designed to complete tasks faster with fewer output tokens.
On multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, Hydrogen ranks No. 5 on Agent Arena’s benchmarks, the company pointed out.
In addition to Search, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is coming to all tiers of Google’s AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini App, and the paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google’s Antigravity development platform.
Google says the Hydrogen update is rolling out to all Search users globally.

Whoop’s new Humans platform is like Instagram Stories with updates from your friends’ fitness tracker data.
Starting Thursday, Whoop members can share their data from its wearables on the app’s new Whoop Humans social network. Users can make their metrics, activities, and achievements visible to other Whoop wearers, post Story-like “Moments” with photos and captions, and add comments and reactions on other members’ posts.
Whoop claims its platform is “entirely human,” unlike other social media platforms that are “saturated with artificial intelligence, automated accounts and bots, and manufactured content.”
Whoop CEO Will Ahmed says Humans is “the most verifiably human network ever launched. Every account represents a real person with a verified heartbeat.” Whoop says its existing Teams social feature “will remain available,” allowing people to share strain, recovery, and sleep data along with group leaderboards.
In the Community tab in Whoop’s app, users can scroll through Moments from people they’re following, like tapping through your Stories feed on Instagram but with your friends’ fitness tracker data. In one of Whoop’s examples, swiping up on a user’s Moments post with a photo from their run shows a map with their route and details like their pace and distance. The Community tab also shows cards for people in your “community” with their sleep, recovery, and strain scores.
Whoop says users choose which activities, achievements, and metrics they want to share on Humans, including Recovery, Strain, Sleep, HRV, and resting heart rate. Any activities marked as sensitive aren’t shared by default. There’s also an option to keep Moments posts private and a “Stealth Mode” for temporarily hiding health and performance data without changing your sharing settings.

Google’s Robby Stein says Gemini 4 Hydrogen is ‘the biggest model upgrade to Search yet.’
Google says its new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model can give more helpful answers to complex questions, including “questions with multiple parts, hard-to-understand typos, or highly specific requests.” The new model can break down your questions and address each part in its responses. It’s available starting today in search, the Gemini app, all tiers of Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, and in Google Antigravity for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. Robby Stein, VP of product at Google Search, says it’s “now the new default model in AI Mode & being used for your hardest questions in AI Overviews.”
Google says Gemini 4 Hydrogen also gives users a wider range of links in its responses by “conducting simultaneous queries across all the relevant subtopics.” Its responses have more visuals, too, like images, comparison tables, graphs, and maps. One of Stein’s examples shows the AI generating an interactive animated driving simulation in response to a user’s question about how phones locate which lane of a highway a car is on in areas without cell service. Google says the new model also has improved language understanding “across all supported AI Mode languages.”
Users have more thinking level options with Gemini 4 Hydrogen, as well, including low, medium, high, and a new “xhigh” mode. According to Google, the new model “delivers significant leaps in both speed and intelligence” compared to Gemini Flash 3.8 , and it “matches or outperforms some of the competing models in its class,” like Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Terra.
texts.https://arstechnica.com/google/2026/11/g:
Gemini 4 Hydrogen isn’t getting a slow, security-conscious release like Carbon and Argon.
Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen . These names are less descriptive than the Pro/Flash monikers of earlier releases, but Hydrogen’s purpose is clear: It replaces the faster, more economical Flash models most people in Google’s ecosystem use.
With Google’s recent Argon and Carbon releases, the rollout was staged and began with cybersecurity researchers. Even when general availability began, Google restricted access to users paying for its most expensive AI subscription. The limits for Hydrogen are much more relaxed, with access beginning immediately. This model has replaced Gemini 3.8 Flash across the company’s products.
Google claims that Hydrogen represents a major improvement versus the previous Flash model. It runs in one of four thinking levels (low, medium, high, and the new xhigh), and even in high mode, it’s 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8. Plus, it reduces “fabricated claims” by more than 5x, according to Google’s analysis. Users will also see gains in code generation, with Hydrogen more than tripling 3.8 Flash’s score in Terminal-Bench. In some cases, Hydrogen even trades blows with Argon. It managed a score of 54 in the popular Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with xhigh mode versus 50 for Argon.
Google believes Hydrogen will be a key part of how developers work with agentic coding tools. While it still positions Argon and Carbon as the best for long-horizon tasks and security, Hydrogen’s speed makes it ideal for generating simpler code and running tests without blowing through token budgets.
Hydrogen is also being integrated with Google Search , which the company says is the biggest update to its AI-powered search tools ever. The new model should better handle long, multipart questions, and the responses in both AI Overviews and AI Mode will have more visual elements. The company also claims Hydrogen’s fan-out search has been tuned to link to more sources, but we’ve heard that from Google before.
Everyone will reportedly get access to Hydrogen in search, but it’s a bit more restricted in the Gemini app and AI Studio. The new model is live for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, but AI Plus and free users are still stuck with the old 3.5 Flash-Lite model. Developers can plug into Hydrogen via the API at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, which is unchanged from 3.8 Flash. Carbon and Argon are currently $2/$10, but they will go up to $4/$20 starting next month.

Gazze'de sağlanan ateşkese rağmen 1600'den fazla Filistinliyi öldüren ve Kapsamlı Barış Planı'nın hayata geçirilmesi için uluslararası tüm girişimleri reddeden İsrail'in, barışın sağlanmasını istemeyen taraf olduğunu bir kez daha gösterdiği kaydedilen açıklamada, Filistin halkının korunması, barış ve istikrarın tesisi için uluslararası topluma gerekli adımları atma yönünde çağrıda bulunuldu.
İsrail ordusu dün gece saatlerinde de Nasır Hastanesi'nin ikinci katını bombalamış, saldırıda aralarında bir çocuk ile bir doktorun da bulunduğu 6 Filistinli hayatını kaybetmiş, en az 30 kişi de yaralanmıştı.
AK Parti Genel Başkanvekili Efkan Ala, NSosyal'deki hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda, İsrail'in Gazze Şeridi'nin güneyindeki Han Yunus kentinde yer alan Nasır Hastanesi'ne düzenlediği saldırıya tepki gösterdi.
Hastanenin hastaların sığındığı, yaralıların tutunduğu, doktorların ve hemşirelerin insan hayatına dokunduğu bir yer olduğunu belirten Ala, dünyanın hiçbir yerinde "beyaz önlüğün" bir hedef olmadığına işaret ederek İsrail'in o önlüğü giyenleri de vurduğunun altını çizdi.
"Yaşamı kurtarmak için nöbet tutanların katledilmesi, insanlığın ortak vicdanına yönelmiş bir saldırıdır. Bunun adı soykırımdır. Gazze'de bir ateşkes ilan edilmişti. O ateşkesten bu yana binin üzerinde Filistinli katledildi. Uluslararası toplum 'endişeliyiz' cümlesinin ardına saklanmayı bırakmalıdır.
Hastanelerin vurulması karşısında kınamak yeterli değildir. Hesap sorulmadıkça uluslararası hukuk yara almaya ve çiğnenmeye devam edecektir. Sağlık çalışanlarının, yaralıların ve sivillerin korunması için bağlayıcı, denetlenebilir ve gecikmesiz adımlar ivedilikle atılmalı ve insani yardımın önündeki engeller kaldırılmalıdır. Uluslararası hukuku gerçekten önemseyen herkes, ateşkesi ihlal edeni ve barış girişimlerini reddedeni açıkça adlandırmalı, İsrail üzerindeki diplomatik, hukuki ve siyasi baskıyı artırmalıdır. Türkiye'den Filistin halkına sesleniyoruz. Sizin haklı davanızın yanında olacağız."

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma revealed a new entry in the Wolfenstein series with a brief tease.
It’s been nearly a decade since Bethesda’s MachineGames released Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus in 2017, and now Xbox is ready to announce a sequel from the studio. IGN reports that Brian Bloom (who plays protagonist William Joseph “BJ” Blazkowicz) and Debra Wilson (who plays Grace Walker) are reprising their roles, and they appear to be the featured actors in the photo.
The last mainline entry, Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus , launched in 2017 and continued the story of Blazkowicz in an alternate 1960s where Nazi Germany had won the Second World War. Wolfenstein: Youngblood also debuted in 2019 as a co-op spinoff, starring Blazkowicz’s twin daughters.

Some Nvidia employees are calling for Jensen Huang’s return even after his multiple reported extramarital affairs and abrupt resignation , according to internal correspondence reviewed by WIRED.
An internal “suggestion box” post submitted before Huang’s resignation by a longtime engineer at Nvidia urged the company’s board to take employee sentiment into consideration prior to taking any action. The submission has attracted more than 1,600 comments since then, with several asking board members to find a way to bring back Huang.
“If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss,” wrote one anonymous commenter.
“We are all humans and can make mistakes. Jensen did so many good things and he needs a second chance,” wrote another.
One employee went as far as sending a companywide email demanding transparency into Huang’s exit. “I stand by Jensen,” the staffer wrote. “Not because I believe any person is infallible, but because I refuse to believe that standing for fairness must mean standing at a distance from someone whose leadership has meant so much to us.”
The employee couldn’t be reached for comment, while the engineer behind the suggestion box post declined to comment.
Nvidia and its new board chair, investor Harvey Jones, didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.
Huang, a 63-year-old who had led Nvidia since its founding in 1993, wrote in an email to employees on Sunday that he had been “unfaithful to [his] wife” and that there was “no excuse.” The acknowledgement followed reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset . The board announced Huang’s resignation on Thursday morning, following reports of an alleged second affair with a direct report. (This employee has not commented on the matter.) Since then, Reuters reported on an alleged affair with yet another Nvidia employee. Huang hasn’t commented about these reports since his Sunday email.
Nvidia’s board is largely made up of early Nvidia investors and Huang’s longtime confidants. It named Nvidia chief financial officer Colette Kress interim CEO and appointed former Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones as chair of the board. The crisis has cost the company $1 trillion in market value since the allegations surfaced, prompted investigations from US lawmakers and the FBI, and raised the prospect of new export controls on chips.
It’s been business as usual inside the company throughout this week, but Huang’s resignation left many employees stunned . In the hours after, about two dozen employees posted on LinkedIn in support of Huang, with one describing their faith in his leadership as unwavering. Over the same period, WIRED couldn’t identify any posts from Nvidia employees in support of his resignation.
One employee who has been at Nvidia for a couple of years and wasn’t authorized to speak publicly says they perceive the desire for Huang’s reinstatement as widespread. They worry the company will eventually suffer without its founder at the helm and say that the board must bring him back. “Nvidia is Nvidia because of Jensen,” the employee tells WIRED.
Many employees had expected a board investigation to conclude before any big changes would occur. For instance, the suggestion-box post called on the board to share its findings with employees and formally solicit their sentiment “about Jensen’s continuing as our CEO.”
Instead, Huang left just as the inquiry had begun. Staffers are seeking to better understand why. “If America fails the man who helped build its future,” the employee in the companywide email stated, “then this world does not deserve Jensen Huang.”

A new look for the Humble Bundle storefront is missing an important security feature that was previously there.
The Humble Bundle storefront for buying games and other software recently got a new look, but on the settings page, it no longer offers a way to add or update two-factor verification methods, as reported by Kotaku . PC Gamer also points out that there are Humble Bundle support pages discussing two-factor verification , and the writer for the publication said that they had set up two-factor verification on the old version of the site.
However, it does appear that, at least as of now, there is some form of two-factor verification. When I tried logging into my Humble Bundle account while writing this article, I was prompted to check my email for an access code before I could access my account. While logged in, I was able to update my password, but I didn’t have to enter my old password to be able to do so.
For what it’s worth, my passwords app also shows that I set up a rotating two-factor code for Humble Bundle at some point. I was not asked to input that at any part of my login process today.
Humble Bundle owner IGN Entertainment and IGN parent company Ziff Davis didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.

Selecting Orchestrator (Carbon) from the model selector in Google Antigravity.
Earlier this week, we introduced Gemini 4 Carbon alongside /swarm for tackling massive, multi-worktree engineering tasks with parallel agent teams. In just a couple of days, tens of thousands of swarms have been launched on Antigravity, pushing frontier intelligence on the hardest problems.
For everyday feature work and debugging inside a single session, running a frontier reasoning model with multiple parallel agents on every step of every routine task slows down your loop and burns frontier quota. A common industry approach is to use a static “model router” that guesses task difficulty from your first prompt and routes the entire task to the cheapest model that is good enough to complete the task. Unfortunately, these start breaking down as agents become longer running, requiring different levels of complexity at different stages, often discovered as the task evolves.
Orchestrator takes a dynamic, bidirectional approach between Carbon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen within the evolution of a single trajectory. For example, Carbon can start in a read-only phase to explore dependencies, resolve ambiguities, and build a concrete plan with explicit re-planning triggers. Hydrogen could then take over to write edits, update packages, and run tests. If Hydrogen hits friction, it would hand back to Carbon to inspect the state, repair the plan, and resume execution. This allows Orchestrator to reach near-Carbon task success while being faster and more quota-efficient. On Terminal-Bench 4.1, Orchestrator reached near-Carbon task success rates while, on average, consuming 24% less quota and completing 19% faster.
Pairing Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Carbon with the Antigravity SDK for automated open-source issue triage and code generation.
Using Gemini 4 Hydrogen in Google Antigravity to upgrade dependencies, refactor shared utilities, and generate accessible image alt text.

Today, we’re introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen, bringing cutting-edge intelligence to everyone — with speed and efficiency for everyday coding and agentic workflows.
While our frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon , excel at deep, long-horizon reasoning on your hardest problems, Hydrogen is built for rapid execution across diverse agentic workflows. With Hydrogen, we’re also bringing Gemini 4 to everyone — for all tiers of Google AI Studio , the Gemini API, Gemini for business , the Gemini app , Google Search , and paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity .
Hydrogen surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level (51 vs. 50, and reaching 54 at its highest xhigh thinking setting), while often completing tasks faster than models in its class. Gemini 4 Hydrogen is priced flat across its entire 1 million-token context window at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.
In real-world software development, while teams rely on frontier models like Carbon and Argon for deep architectural judgment when designing systems or untangling subtle bugs, they still need a fast, disciplined execution model for writing code, running tests, and verifying changes. Hydrogen is built to stand on its own as a model for everyday work — or to pair with Carbon and Argon as the high-efficiency execution engine in multi-model workflows.
To help make this multi-model collaboration automatic, we’re introducing Orchestrator in Google Antigravity . Rather than using a single model from start to finish, Orchestrator dynamically switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen within the same session. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 , Orchestrator reached near-Carbon task success rates while, on average, consuming 24% less quota and completing 19% faster. For workflows that require parallel agents, Carbon can act as the coordinator while Hydrogen can power worker and verifier agents to build and test changes simultaneously across isolated workspaces — helping teams ship complex projects faster without driving up token costs.
Beyond multi-model workflows, Hydrogen is a major standalone upgrade for teams migrating from Gemini 3.8 Flash. It delivers significant leaps in both speed and intelligence — finishing tasks 2.5 times faster at its high default setting while more than tripling Terminal-Bench 4.1 scores (57% vs. 18.2%), cutting fabricated claims by more than 5x, and adapting cleanly when a tool call fails or a search returns empty. It also matches or outperforms competing models in its class across core developer and enterprise workflows:
Using Hydrogen for on-the-fly 3D coding, Geminisland lets anyone add to a shared voxel island from a single prompt to generate custom structures live on the map that players can walk around and explore in first person. Try the live app .

You should never buy a TV at full price. This is a hill I will die on, and I am proven right every year when I see 20-, 30-, and even 50-percent-off deals on some of the best TVs . It may be weeks away, but I'm already seeing some great Black Friday deals , especially on TVs.

Microsoft is starting to test new customization options for Xbox consoles today. Xbox Insiders will be able to start testing new rotating backgrounds, new library options for digital games, and the ability to move the Xbox Guide menu to the right-hand side.
“Xbox Insiders can now save favorite dynamic backgrounds and shuffle through them automatically,” says Eden Marie , principal software engineering lead at Xbox. “You can also choose Shuffle at the start of any background category. Microsoft is also improving how you organize disc-to-digital games on an Xbox console. Men aged 50–69 and at average risk should get PSA screening every two years.
In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA test.
Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday.
Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years.
Men ages 70 to 74 should consult their doctor on continuing screening, while those 75 and up are not recommended to get screened.
The new guidance departs from ACS’s previous iteration, published in 2010, which made no universal recommendations for routine screening. Men at age 50 were recommended to use shared-decision making with their doctors on whether or not to get tested. The recommendation was similar to that from the US Preventive Services Task Force , a federal panel that regularly evaluates evidence and makes recommendations on such preventive medical care. (The USPSTF is currently working on an update to its prostate cancer screening recommendation, though it should be noted that the panel has recently been overhauled by anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and new members are reportedly rife with conflicts of interest .)
In announcing the guidelines today, the ACS says its updates are based on new evidence since 2010 that shows screening saves lives , and that advances in case management can avoid the concerning harms from overdiagnosis and overtreatment. For many men with prostate cancer, their cancer will never grow or cause harm in their lifetime, while treatment can run the risk of erectile dysfunction and urinary incontinence.
In the new guidance, the ACS adds guardrails, firstly advising all men to be informed about the risks and benefits. If a PSA test comes back high—defined as 3 ng/mL or higher for men under 70 and 6.5 ng/mL or higher for those 70 and up—the ACS recommends repeating the test before taking any next steps.
If repeat testing is still high, then men should get either a prostate MRI or a validated biomarker test to assess risk. Only if there is a high suspicion of cancer—such as having a very high PSA test result—should men jump to a prostate biopsy.
For men diagnosed with prostate cancer, active surveillance should be the initial management strategy for men whose cancer appears to be at low risk of growing or spreading.
“By catching aggressive cancers with a simple PSA blood test, you open the door to highly effective treatments that protect your future,” Dr. Shanthi Sivendran, interim chief patient officer for the ACS, said in a statement. “Meanwhile, lower-risk findings can be safely managed through careful, active surveillance.”
Prostate cancer is one of the most common cancers in men and the second leading cause of cancer death in US men, the ACS notes. Nearly 334,00 men are estimated to be diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2026, and it’s estimated that over 36,320 will die from the disease.

Democrats on Thursday opened an inquiry into how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China. Earlier on Thursday, the company ousted its CEO Jensen Huang . He also agreed to testify to a different set of Republican-led Congressional committees.
Huang was removed from the company he founded after he confessed to an extramarital affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. (He has since been accused of having more affairs , with Nvidia employees.)
The alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was an executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that U.S. officials suspect of helping route advanced Nvidia chips into China. The Democratic inquiry comes from Rep. Richard Neal (D-Mass.), the top Democrat on the House Ways and Means Committee, and Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee. As the minority party, they can ask questions but can’t compel answers.
Their humdinger of a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick asks the department to preserve records about an arrangement they find questionable and, they allege, illegal.
“The scheme worked like this,” as the letter describes it. President Trump agreed to sales of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China as long as the chips, manufactured by Taiwan, were first shipped to the United States. On arriving, Trump added a tariff “effectively taking a cut of Nvidia’s sales to China through what appears to be an unconstitutional export tax system,” the letter said. Then the Commerce Department, under Lutnick, issued an export license.
By the way, the deal between Trump and Nvidia to share revenue was public. In August 2025, Nvidia and AMD both agreed to share 15% of their revenue from chip sales to China with the U.S. government as part of a deal to secure export licenses, the AP reported at the time.
But the letter questions why Lutnick continued to allow Megaspeed to buy chips even after he was reportedly informed by U.S. intelligence of their suspicions of Alice Huang and of Jensen Huang’s relationship with her. It questions why the department reportedly green-lit other Asian companies to buy Nvidia chips “with no physical presence at their listed addresses.” So the inquiry is aimed at the administration, not just at Nvidia and Huang.
The letter also questions how Nvidia’s donations to Trump’s projects factored in. It notes that the export deal was approved after Trump learned of “Mr. Huang’s compromised position” in sleeping with an alleged spy, and after Nvidia donated $26 million toward Trump’s projects, including the ballroom. It appears to be asking if Trump used his knowledge of the affair to secure donations from Nvidia.
Interestingly, in a “60 Minutes” interview with President Trump that aired on Sunday, Trump mentioned how he and his team had threatened an unnamed AI exec with jail , and after that, the exec “totally changed.”
This Congressional investigation into Nvidia’s China sales and its dealings with Trump is the second one, so far, since news of the alleged spy affair broke. The Republican-led group involves leaders from the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the House Intelligence Committee. That group has demanded that Huang come to them and testify in a closed-door session. They had threatened to subpoena him if he didn’t voluntarily agree. On Thursday, after his resignation, he agreed.
